question: What is the primary purpose of a questionnaire in nursing research?

options.A: Prescribing routine medications to stable clients
options.B: Diagnosing complex medical conditions in patients
options.C: Gathering structured data directly from participants
options.D: Replacing physical examinations in the hospital ward

explanation: Questionnaires are standardized tools designed specifically to collect systematic information from a target population. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why are questionnaires particularly useful for clinical nursing studies in busy hospital settings?

options.A: They completely remove human bias from the research process
options.B: They guarantee that every single respondent will return the form
options.C: They allow efficient collection of data without disrupting patient care
options.D: They eliminate the need for any formal ethical committee approval

explanation: Their structured format enables researchers to gather large amounts of standardized data quickly in active healthcare environments. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h1)

question: Which item type requires respondents to write answers in their own words?
explanation: Open-ended questions allow participants to express their views freely without being restricted to predefined choices. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h2)

question: A researcher wants to measure patient satisfaction levels on a five-point scale from poor to excellent. What item format should be used?
explanation: Likert scales are specifically designed to measure attitudes, opinions, or perception levels along a structured continuum. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h2)

question: What is a double-barreled question in a research instrument?

options.A: A question that forces the participant to tell a lie
options.B: A question that asks about two different things at once
options.C: A question translated into two different local languages
options.D: A question with only two possible answer choices

explanation: Double-barreled items confuse respondents because they cannot answer both parts of the query independently. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h3)

question: How should sensitive or personal questions be arranged within a survey layout?

options.A: Omitted entirely to prevent any possible participant bias
options.B: Placed at the very beginning to get them out of the way
options.C: Placed later after rapport and trust are established
options.D: Spread randomly throughout every page of the document

explanation: Starting with easy, non-threatening items helps build respondent confidence before tackling sensitive subjects. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h3)

question: What does the reliability of a questionnaire refer to?

options.A: Accuracy of measuring the true intended concept
options.B: Simplicity of language used in the instructions
options.C: Approval of the document by an ethics committee
options.D: Consistency of results when repeated over time

explanation: Reliability indicates that the measurement tool produces stable and dependable scores across repeated administrations. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h4)

question: A nurse researcher calculates a Cronbach's alpha of 0.85 for a new anxiety scale. What does this value indicate?

options.B: High rate of missing survey responses
options.C: Excessive bias in the sample selection

explanation: A Cronbach's alpha value above 0.70 generally indicates acceptable to high internal consistency among scale items. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h4)

question: Which administration mode is most suitable for respondents with low literacy levels?
explanation: Having an interviewer read the items aloud assists participants who struggle with reading or writing. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is a major advantage of utilizing digital web-based questionnaires?

options.A: Total elimination of internet connectivity challenges
options.B: Complete absence of sampling bias in the population
options.C: Rapid data collection and automated electronic entry
options.D: Guaranteed 100 percent response rate from the public

explanation: Online platforms collect and compile responses instantly, bypassing manual data entry errors. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a pilot test for a questionnaire?

options.A: Securing financial grants from hospital management boards
options.B: Identifying ambiguous items and operational flaws before the main study
options.C: Publishing the final research findings in an international journal
options.D: Recruiting all actual participants needed for the final project

explanation: Piloting detects hidden errors and unclear wording so adjustments can be made prior to full data collection. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h6)

question: Who should comprise the sample group used for testing a draft questionnaire?

options.A: Individuals with characteristics similar to the actual target population
options.B: Expert statisticians and senior hospital administrative directors
options.C: Patients admitted to intensive care units with critical illnesses
options.D: First-year nursing students who have never studied research methods

explanation: The pilot group must closely mirror the intended study participants to accurately reveal comprehension issues and timing problems. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h6)

question: What does maintaining participant anonymity in a survey involve?

options.A: Ensuring no names or identifying details are linked to responses
options.B: Publishing the real identities of respondents alongside data
options.C: Sharing raw completed forms with hospital ward managers
options.D: Storing physical questionnaire papers in unlocked staff rooms

explanation: Anonymity means even the researcher cannot trace a specific questionnaire back to an individual participant. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h7)

question: A patient agrees to answer a questionnaire in the clinic waiting room. What right do they maintain throughout the process?

options.A: The privilege of receiving financial payment for answers
options.B: The obligation to finish every question on the form
options.C: The right to withdraw at any time without penalty
options.D: The authority to change hospital admission policies

explanation: Participation in research must remain voluntary, and individuals can stop answering whenever they choose. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of using questionnaires in research?

options.A: They allow easy probing of complex emotional nuances in real-time
options.B: They are cost-effective when reaching large numbers of people
options.C: They provide a standardized format that reduces interviewer bias
options.D: They offer convenience for respondents to complete at their own pace

explanation: Static questionnaires lack the flexibility to probe deeper into complex answers, unlike face-to-face qualitative interviews. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h8)

question: What is a frequent challenge encountered with mailed or self-administered surveys?

options.A: Excessive costs incurred from hiring trained interviewers
options.B: Too much qualitative data that takes years to analyze
options.C: Low response rates leading to potential non-response bias
options.D: High risk of physical injury to participating hospital staff

explanation: Many distributed questionnaires are never returned, which can skew results if respondents differ systematically from non-respondents. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h8)
